speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To understand your chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination, I need to clarify the nature of your symptoms. Have you experienced any pain specifically during urination or blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The relief of discomfort after voiding and dyspareunia (painful intercourse) alongside frequency strongly suggests a gynecological or local pelvic inflammatory cause rather than simple overactive bladder. Has your menstrual cycle been regular, and do you have any history of sexually transmitted infections or recent new sexual partners?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.

The relief of symptoms after voiding and the chronic nature of the pain despite NSAIDs are classic for Interstitial Cystitis. To confirm this and rule out other causes, please provide results for a Urinalysis with microscopy and a Renal Ultrasound of the bladder.
